## Summary

Harman Becker Automotive Systems grew out of a repair workshop founded in Pforzheim in 1949, has its head office in Karlsbad near Karlsruhe, was taken over by Harman International in 1995, and makes car radios, navigation systems, voice control, human-machine interfaces and audio and entertainment systems [3]. Harman International, headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, has been an independent subsidiary of Samsung Electronics since March 2017 and lists Becker as its car infotainment brand [4]. The IEEE registry lists ten MA-L blocks to Harman/Becker Automotive Systems GmbH, nine at Becker-Goering-Strasse 16, Karlsbad, and one at Stamford, Connecticut, and an IAB block at Karlsbad [1][2].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely a car head unit: Harman Becker has supplied Mercedes-Benz from its earliest days and also lists Audi, Peugeot, Hyundai, Ferrari, Rolls-Royce, Porsche, BMW and MINI as customers [3]. Expect it on the air when a vehicle offers a hotspot or phone pairing, but the sources consulted document neither its radios nor its silicon, so both are empty rather than assumed. FCC grantee codes are not listed because the FCC ID databases refused access from the session that wrote this entry; no advisory naming this company was found, and randomization is unknown.
